original_question: Let ∼g denote subgroup conjugacy inside a semigroup, let U(S) be the group of units, and let ∼u be unit conjugacy. If one also requires Green’s H-relation, so that one compares ∼u ∩ H with ∼g, are these two relations equal for every semigroup having fewer than 13 elements?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Example 4.4: the paper leaves open whether (∼u ∩ H) = ∼g for all semigroups of size less than 13; this is the nearest official formulation of your draft, rather than the broader inclusion diagram of Theorem 4.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right local open problem, the correct two relations being compared, and the correct finite-size cutoff |S| < 13. It also stays narrowly focused on the paper’s Section 4 discussion instead of drifting to a broader neighboring problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
missing_details: State the quantifier explicitly: the question is over every finite semigroup S with |S| < 13, and equality means equality of binary relations on S.
Define subgroup conjugacy exactly as in Section 2: for a,b ∈ S, a ∼g b means either a = b, or there exists a subgroup G ≤ S containing both a and b and an element g ∈ G such that g^{-1}ag = b.
Define unit conjugacy exactly as used in Section 4: for a,b ∈ S, a ∼u b iff there exists g ∈ U(S) such that g^{-1}ag = b and gbg^{-1} = a.
Spell out Green’s H-relation: a H b iff a L b and a R b.
Make clear that the relation being compared with ∼g is the intersection ∼u ∩ H, not bare unit conjugacy ∼u.
Clarify that the question is motivated by Example 4.4, which gives a 13-element semigroup witnessing failure at size 13, so the issue is whether any counterexample can occur below 13.
refined_question: For every finite semigroup S with |S| < 13, is the relation (∼u ∩ H) equal to subgroup conjugacy ∼g on S? Here, for a,b ∈ S, a ∼g b means that either a = b or there exists a subgroup G ≤ S containing a and b together with an element g ∈ G such that g^{-1}ag = b; a ∼u b means that there exists g ∈ U(S) such that g^{-1}ag = b and gbg^{-1} = a; and H is Green’s H-relation, i.e. a H b iff a L b and a R b.
justification: Section 2 supplies the paper’s definition of subgroup conjugacy ∼g. Section 4 then defines unit conjugacy ∼u, recalls Green’s H-relation, and explains that H can be intersected with the various conjugacies. Example 4.4 is the precise place where the paper states the open question matching your draft: after exhibiting a 13-element semigroup relevant to this comparison, the author asks whether (∼u ∩ H) = ∼g for all semigroups of size less than 13. That makes Example 4.4, not the entire Theorem 4.1 diagram, the closest paper-faithful target. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
